payload.claim:
`_CRITERION`'s lookahead `(?=
[ 	]*-\s*\[[ xX]\]|\Z)` terminates a criterion's captured span only at the next checklist marker or the end of the section, not at the actual boundary of that criterion's indented wrapped lines. Because `\s*` and `.+?` are DOTALL/whitespace-matching, any non-checklist content between two items — e.g. a blank line followed by a stray note or explanatory paragraph that is not indented as a continuation — is silently absorbed into the *previous* criterion's claim (verified by hand-tracing: `- [ ] first

Note: commentary.

- [ ] second` yields a first claim of "first Note: commentary."). This is broader than the stated intent ("a wrapped criterion's continuation lines belong to it") and than the acceptance criterion ("joins a wrapped acceptance criterion into one string"): it joins anything up to the next `- [ ]`, not just genuine wrapped continuation lines. Since `acceptance_criteria` text is exactly what a future refusal gate (`SA-0016`, named in this spec's own rationale) scans for path tokens, a garbled merge like this can inject or obscure a path token that was never really part of that criterion's claim.
